title: Numerical Simulations of Warp Drive Atmospheric Signatures: Terawatt-Scale Luminosities from Relativistic Shock Heating
abstract: Fell & Loeb simulate Alcubierre-type warp bubbles traversing Earth's atmosphere. At 0.5c, shock heating reaches 220 billion Kelvin, producing terawatt-scale luminosities. Slow-moving orbs (~m/s) at micrometer scales could represent miniature warp bubbles with dramatically reduced signatures. The 'mother orb' phenomenon (smaller orbs launched from larger) remains unexplained by conventional aerodynamics.

c9_implications.detection: High-speed warp signatures would be unmissable. Slow micrometer orbs are the only physically viable 'stealth' configuration.
c9_implications.uap_relevance: Pentagon orbs (slow, small) fit the micrometer-scale parameter space. No known propulsion mechanism explains non-Newtonian motion at these scales.
c9_implications.theoretical_status: Alcubierre metric requires exotic matter (negative energy density). No known material can sustain the required stress-energy tensor.
